title: Coherent Magnons Driven by Photomodulated Anisotropy in Altermagnetic MnTe
authors: Dingbin Huang, Jonathon Kruppe, Resham Babu Regmi, Nirmal J. Ghimire, James Analytis, Joseph Orenstein
abstract: Manganese telluride ($\text{MnTe}$) has recently emerged as a prototypical $g$-wave altermagnet, providing an ideal platform to investigate the non-equilibrium excitations of altermagnetic order. Here, we report simultaneous spatial mapping of the local equilibrium orientation of the Néel vector, $\varphi_L(\mathbf{r})$, alongside the amplitude, $Δ\varphi(\mathbf{r},t)$, and frequency, $Ω(\mathbf{r})$, of photoexcited spin waves. Based on these measurements, we place a remarkably low upper bound of $\approx 60~μ\text{eV}$ (0.7 K) on the spin-wave gap arising from intrinsic anisotropy. This exceptionally weak hexagonal anisotropy ($K_6$) renders the altermagnetic order highly susceptible to optical tuning, allowing coherent spin waves to be driven by a photoinduced enhancement of $K_6$. Above a threshold pump fluence, our spatial maps reveal that this photomodulation manifests as a six-fold symmetric sawtooth dependence of $Δ\varphi$ on $\varphi_L$ and a cycloid-like modulation of $Ω$. Ultimately, the near-isotropy of the Néel vector in $\text{MnTe}$ enables optical and mechanical control over the orientation of spin-splitting in the electronic band structure, offering new pathways for altermagnetic spintronics.
summary: This work uses time-resolved optical measurements on altermagnetic MnTe to study magnon excitations. By mapping the dependence of spin wave properties on pump laser fluence, the authors show that the material's anisotropy can be optically modulated. This opens new avenues for controlling electronic band structure via magnetic order in spintronics.
main_problem: The study investigates coherent magnon dynamics driven by photomodulated anisotropy in altermagnetic MnTe, aiming to understand how external tuning controls magnetic order and electronic band structure.
main_result: The research demonstrated that above a pump fluence threshold, the system exhibits characteristic six-fold symmetric sawtooth dependence of spin wave amplitude and cycloid modulation of frequency, enabling optical control over spin splitting.
method: Time-resolved polarimetry was used to spatially map local equilibrium Néel vector orientation ($\varphi_L$) alongside photoexcited spin wave amplitude ($\Delta\varphi$) and frequency ($\Omega$).
model_or_system: The system is MnTe, a prototypical g-wave altermagnet. The dynamics are modeled using a free energy landscape incorporating 6-fold anisotropy ($K_6$) and 2-fold magneto-elastic coupling ($K_2$).
key_observables: Local equilibrium Néel vector orientation ($\varphi_L$), photoexcited spin wave amplitude ($\Delta\varphi$), and magnon frequency ($\Omega$).
important_parameters: Intrinsic anisotropy upper bound of $\approx 60 \mu	ext{eV}$ (0.7 K); critical pump fluence threshold; temperature regimes (low vs. high T).
main_assumptions: The low-T analysis suggests strain inhomogeneity dominates, while the high-T model assumes photoexcitation induces a modulation of $K_6$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structure and pump-probe setups; key results show fluence dependence leading to sawtooth patterns in $\Delta\varphi$ and cycloid variations in $\Omega$ at higher temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical system (altermagnetism) to detailing measurement techniques (time-resolved polarimetry), presenting low-T vs. high-T dynamics, and finally quantifying the photomodulation effects on anisotropy parameters ($K_6$).
why_interesting: The ability to optically tune magnetic anisotropies in a material with zero net magnetization provides an excellent platform for studying non-equilibrium spin dynamics, which has parallels in driven quantum systems.
